veranderings.voor: Die meeste van die land is
veranderings.na: Die grootste deel van die land is
veranderings.rede: 'Die meeste van die land' follows English 'most of the country'; 'die grootste deel' is the idiomatic Afrikaans for a portion of one area.

veranderings.blok: Die Nyl het elke jaar oorstroom
veranderings.voor: Die Aswan-hoogdam beheer sedert 1970 die rivier.
veranderings.na: Sedert 1970 beheer die Aswan-hoogdam die rivier.
veranderings.rede: Putting the time phrase first reads more naturally and links better to the next sentence starting with 'Vandag'.

veranderings.na: In hierdie strook het nedersettings gegroei:
veranderings.rede: 'Daar' follows a sentence about the desert, so it can be read as pointing to the desert instead of the strip along the river.
'Daardie' is stiff and distancing for boats just mentioned; the plain article reads more naturally.

veranderings.voor: 'n groot en georganiseerde samelewing met landbou en handel en ook 'n regering en godsdiens
veranderings.na: 'n groot, georganiseerde samelewing met landbou, handel, 'n regering en godsdiens
veranderings.rede: The chain of 'en ... en ook ... en' is clumsy; a plain list reads better and matches the glossary definition of beskawing word for word.

veranderings.na: en die land rondom die rivier bedek
veranderings.rede: 'Rondom' left without an object reads as incomplete; naming the river makes the definition clear when read on its own.
